chains.notes: No published nutrition found for Egon. Checked egon.no, /menyen, /nymeny and a site-restricted search. None show kcal or macro values or link to a nutrition or allergen PDF. Reviews say an allergen overview exists as a printed or in-restaurant menu, but it has no nutrition values and is not online. Searches for Sweden, Denmark and UK data found nothing (Egon is a Norwegian chain). No items returned, since values must not be estimated.

No official nutrition found for Dolly Dimple's. dolly.no has no nutrition page or PDF; its FAQ says to ask the store about allergens/ingredients. Product pages on dolly.no (e.g. /product/10013) list only allergens and price, and redirect to the order.ninito.com menu, which returned no menu text or nutrition when fetched (it may be JS-rendered, so I could not rule out values behind it). Searches found no nutrition PDF. The chain is Norway-only, so there is no SE/DK/UK backup. The only values seen were third-party user-entered entries on mylog.no (e.g. Bankers 213 kcal/100 g, 125 g portion). I did not use them because they are not published by the chain and the snippet was incomplete. Returning no items rather than guessing.

No items returned. joejuice.com (Norwegian pages and /allergens) answered HTTP 429 on every WebFetch (4 tries), so I could not read any official nutrition page. Searches found no official Norwegian nutrition PDF. Only third-party values turned up: mylog.no (Norwegian user diary, e.g. Pick me up 180 kcal per 340 g), FatSecret, fddb and Deliveroo UK listings. They are crowd-sourced or from other countries and conflict with each other (Joe's Club Sandwich 415 to 449 kcal per 100 g, 430 kcal per serving), so I did not use them. The official source to retry is https://www.joejuice.com/allergens, with the Norwegian menu pages, later or from a browser tool. A 2021 airport menu PDF (US) exists but is old and not Norwegian.

Source: per-product nutrition pages on kaffebrenneriet.no (/mat-kategori/naeringsinnhold?ProductID=...). They print only per 100 g plus "Vekt ca X g"; no per-portion values are printed, so per_portion is all null (not computed). Drinks and coffee drinks pages have no nutrition published. Not collected: ice cream, chocolate and cookies categories, other scones, muffins, tekake sjokolade, pepperkakebar, hasselnøttbar, KokoKrønsj, Speltgrøt, Kaldgrøt. Gulrotkake (1252 g), Sjokoladekake (1136 g) and Suksesskake (800 g) list the weight of a whole cake, so sure=false. Kardemommebolle at 175 g looks high, sure=false. Kcal values copied as printed (with decimals); kJ omitted.

chains.notes: No items returned: I could not read full nutrition tables. Waynes product pages exist (waynescoffee.no/produkt/... and waynescoffee.com/product/...) and seem to carry nutrition and allergens per product, but the site is a JavaScript single-page app (Base44). WebFetch returns only the page title, and waynescoffee.no fails with a TLS error. waynes.se refuses connections. I found no nutrition PDF. I stopped probing the site's JS bundle and API after the permission system denied that step. WebSearch snippets mention values for some items (for example apple pie 248 kcal per portion / 230 per 100 g, blueberry cheesecake 405 / 300, scones 577 / 828, ciabatta chicken and bacon 649, spinach and feta pie 710, Caesar salad about 510). These are summaries, partly Swedish site, with no complete nutrient set or portion weights, so I did not record them. To finish: render the product pages in a headless browser, or ask Waynes for a nutrition sheet. Candidate pages: waynescoffee.no/produkt/supercino-rodbeta/, and on waynescoffee.com: appelpaj, blabarscheesecake, kanelbulle, lasagne, caesarsallad, raksallad, cookieshake, wrap-med-kyckling-cashewrora, ciabatta-med-kyckling-bacon, paj-med-spenat-fetaost, scones-med-cream-cheese-marmelad.

Godt Brød is a bakery chain, not a restaurant. Norwegian product pages on godtbrod.no print nutrition per 100 g only. No piece or loaf weights and no per-portion values are printed, so per_portion is empty, portion_g is null and every item is sure=false. No nutrition PDF found. Values were read via WebFetch summaries of the pages and may carry transcription risk. Several pages show identical values (Kanelknute vs Skillingsbolle; Loff vs Rundstykke lyst), possibly copied. Mandelcroissant and Sesamrundstykke have empty nutrition sections. Salt is the printed salt figure (sodium also printed). Coffee drinks and other breads (Frørik, Sesambrød, Lørdagsbrød, etc.) were not fetched. No backup-country data was used.

Remaining Baker Hansen pages (breads, other buns, scones) were not all checked, so more nutrition may exist on a few of them.

chains.notes: No nutrition data found for TGI Fridays Norway. fridays.no menu pages (main-menu, lunch-menu, drinks-menu, afterwork_menu) list allergens in Norwegian only, with no kcal, no nutrition values, no portion weights and no nutrition PDF links. Searches for a Norwegian nutrition or allergen PDF found nothing. A UK backup exists: tgifridays.co.uk menu PDFs print kcal per dish only (no protein, fat, carbs, salt or portion weights, as far as search snippets show), and the UK recipes and menu differ from Norway (for example, the Mozzarella Dippers kcal changed between UK menu versions). The UK Core PDF could not be parsed by WebFetch (binary stream). Because kcal-only UK values cannot be matched to the current Norwegian menu and have no portion weights, I returned no items rather than guess. Third-party sites (mylog, fatsecret) are user-maintained and were not used. Possible follow-up: extract UK PDF text with pdftotext (saved copy at C:\Users\Admin\.claude\projects\C--Users-Admin-Documents-Claude-Github-Makro\1869626e-2a48-4b10-b394-c99638cb99e3\tool-results\webfetch-1794586482995-dgvuyj.pdf) and import kcal-only UK items with sure=false if wanted.

No items collected. Norway does publish a nutrition PDF: https://burgerking.no/services/pdf/download/nutrition (found via search; the snippet says it is about 1,181 days old, so roughly 3 years). burgerking.no is an Angular single-page app. WebFetch and a plain download returned only the empty HTML shell (4,350 bytes, content-type text/html), not the PDF or its data. I tried to read the site's JavaScript bundle for the underlying API or PDF path, but the permission classifier denied that action, so I stopped and did not work around it. burgerking.se is the same kind of app shell, and I found no Swedish, Danish or UK Burger King nutrition PDF. Only third-party figures turned up (mylog.no, MyFitnessPal, fatsecret, spisetips.no, US-based sites). They conflict with each other (for example, Whopper 608 to 678 kcal) and none is the chain's own printed data, so I did not use them. Burger King Lithuania (burgerking.lt) and Cyprus (burgerking.com.cy) publish per-item nutrition on their menu pages. I did not use them because they are outside the allowed backup countries (SE, DK, UK). Suggested next step: have a person with a browser download the Norwegian PDF, or allow reading burgerking.no's JS bundle to find the PDF or API URL, then re-run.

Sabi Sushi: no nutrition published. sabi.no and nettbutikk.sabi.no have a JS-rendered menu and an allergen page (/allergener) with no kcal or macros; no nutrition PDF found; search found only allergen tags per dish. No items returned for Sabi.
Yo! Sushi: has an Oslo restaurant (Østbanehallen) but I found no Norwegian nutrition source (yosushi.no does not resolve). The only published numbers are the UK Yo! Sushi dine-in allergen and nutrition page (menus.tenkites.com/yosushi/allergenpageyosushi). It gives per-serving values, no portion weights and no per 100 g. All items are backup data from GB with sure=false, and it is not confirmed they are on the Norwegian menu. Source columns: kJ, kcal, fat, saturates, sugars, salt, protein, carb, starch, fibre. Values were parsed from page text by script, so a name-to-row mismatch is possible (popcorn shrimp the least certain). Not included: items where the name could not be matched reliably (for example prawn crackers had two differing rows).
